fields.question:
A ball is thrown upwards and its height h (in metres) after t seconds is given by h = −5t² + 20t.
(i) After how many seconds does the ball hit the ground?
(ii) At what times is the ball at a height of 15 m?
(iii) For what value of k will −5t² + 20t = k have equal roots? Hence find the greatest height reached by the ball and the time at which it is reached.
fields.answer: (i) t = 4 s. (ii) t = 1 s and t = 3 s. (iii) k = 20; greatest height 20 m, reached at t = 2 s.
fields.explanation: Each part is solved as a quadratic equation: h = 0 for landing, h = 15 for the given height, and equal roots (D = 0) for the single highest point.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) h = 0 ⟹ −5t² + 20t = 0 ⟹ 5t(4 − t) = 0 ⟹ t = 0 (launch) or t = 4. The ball hits the ground after 4 s.
[1 mark] (ii) −5t² + 20t = 15 ⟹ t² − 4t + 3 = 0 ⟹ (t − 1)(t − 3) = 0 ⟹ t = 1 s (going up) and t = 3 s (coming down).
[1 mark] (iii) 5t² − 20t + k = 0 has equal roots when D = (−20)² − 4(5)(k) = 400 − 20k = 0 ⟹ k = 20.
[1 mark] (iii) With k = 20 the ball reaches that height only once, so it is the greatest height, 20 m; the equal root t = 20/(2 × 5) = 2 s.
fields.finalAnswer: (i) 4 s; (ii) 1 s and 3 s; (iii) k = 20; greatest height 20 m at t = 2 s.

fields.questionText: Prove that √5 is an irrational number.
fields.answer: Assuming √5 = p/q (p, q co-prime integers, q ≠ 0) leads to 5 dividing both p and q, contradicting co-primality. Hence √5 is irrational.

[1 mark] Then 25a² = 5q² ⇒ q² = 5a², so 5 divides q², hence 5 divides q.
[1 mark] So 5 is a common factor of p and q, contradicting that p and q are co-prime. Hence √5 is irrational.

Two rectangular sheets, each of dimensions 45 cm × 155 cm, are folded to make hollow right circular cylindrical pipes, with exactly 1 cm overlap when sticking the ends. Sheet 1 is folded along its length (so its height is 155 cm) and Sheet 2 along its width (so its height is 45 cm). Both pipes are closed at both ends.
(i) Find the difference in the curved surface areas of the two cylinders.
(ii) Find the ratio of the volumes of the two cylinders formed. (Use π = 22/7.)
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Sheet 1: height h₁ = 155 cm, circumference = 45 − 1 = 44 cm. Sheet 2: height h₂ = 45 cm, circumference = 155 − 1 = 154 cm.
[1 mark] (i) CSA = circumference × height: CSA₁ = 44 × 155 = 6820 cm², CSA₂ = 154 × 45 = 6930 cm²; difference = 6930 − 6820 = 110 cm².
[1 mark] (ii) 2πr₁ = 44 ⟹ r₁ = 7 cm; 2πr₂ = 154 ⟹ r₂ = 49/2 cm.
fields.strategyHint: The side along which the sheet is folded becomes the height; the other side minus the 1 cm overlap becomes the circumference.

fields.questionText:
A teacher sets up a geometry problem: In △ABC, points D and E are marked on sides AB and AC respectively. It is given that DE ∥ BC. The teacher asks students to find relationships between the segments.
(i) If AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 1.5 cm, find EC.
(ii) Are △ADE and △ABC similar? Justify using an appropriate criterion.
(iii) If, further, BC = 5 cm, find the length of DE.
fields.answer: (i) 2.25 cm (ii) Yes, by AA criterion (corresponding angles equal) (iii) DE = 2 cm
solutionSteps: (i) Since DE ∥ BC, by BPT: AD/DB = AE/EC ⇒ 2/3 = 1.5/EC ⇒ EC = 4.5/2 = 2.25 cm. [1 mark]
(ii) DE ∥ BC ⇒ ∠ADE = ∠ABC and ∠AED = ∠ACB (corresponding angles); hence △ADE ~ △ABC by AA criterion. [1 mark]
(iii) AB = AD + DB = 5 cm; from △ADE ~ △ABC, DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/5. [1 mark]
fields.finalAnswer: (i) 2.25 cm (ii) Yes, by AA criterion (iii) DE = 2 cm

Ravi, standing on the roof of a house, is holding the string straight and observes the angle of elevation of the kite as 30°. From the bottom of the same building, the angle of elevation of the kite is 45°. Find the length of the string and the height of the roof from the ground. (Use √3 = 1.73)
fields.answer: Length of the string = 40√3 m ≈ 69.2 m; height of the roof = (60 − 20√3) m ≈ 25.4 m

[1 mark] From T: tan 45° = KG/GT ⇒ 1 = 60/GT ⇒ GT = 60 m, so SR = 60 m.
[1 mark] From R: tan 30° = KS/SR ⇒ 1/√3 = KS/60 ⇒ KS = 20√3 m ≈ 34.6 m.
[1 mark] Height of roof TR = 60 − 20√3 = 60 − 34.6 = 25.4 m.
[1 mark] sin 30° = KS/KR ⇒ 1/2 = 20√3/KR ⇒ KR = 40√3 = 69.2 m. Length of string = 69.2 m; height of roof = 25.4 m.
fields.finalAnswer: Length of the string = 69.2 m; height of the roof from the ground = 25.4 m

From the top of a lighthouse 40 m high, a coast guard observes two boats on the same straight line with the base of the lighthouse, on the same side of it. The angles of depression of the boats are 45° and 30°.
(i) Find the distance of the nearer boat (angle of depression 45°) from the base of the lighthouse. [1 mark]
(ii) Find the distance of the farther boat (angle of depression 30°) from the base of the lighthouse. [1 mark]
(iii) Find the distance between the two boats. (Use √3 = 1.732) [2 marks]
fields.explanation: The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles). Use tan in each right triangle with the 40 m height, then subtract the two distances.
solutionSteps: (i) Angle of elevation from nearer boat = 45°: tan 45° = 40/x ⇒ x = 40 m. [1]
(ii) Angle of elevation from farther boat = 30°: tan 30° = 40/y ⇒ 1/√3 = 40/y ⇒ y = 40√3 m ≈ 69.28 m. [1]
(iii) Boats are on the same side, so distance between them = y − x = 40√3 − 40. [1]

fields.questionText:
A boy is standing at a point A on level ground such that the angle of elevation of the top of a school building is 45°. When he walks 20 m closer to the building to a point B, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. Let the height of the building be h m and the distance of A from the foot of the building be x m.
(i) Using the observation from A, express h in terms of x. [1 mark]
(ii) Using the observation from B, form an equation in x. [1 mark]
(iii) Find the height of the building, correct to one decimal place. (Use √3 = 1.732) [2 marks]
fields.finalAnswer: (i) h = x; (ii) √3(x − 20) = x; (iii) Height of the building = 10(3 + √3) ≈ 47.3 m.
solutionSteps: (i) At A: tan 45° = h/x ⇒ 1 = h/x ⇒ h = x. [1]
(ii) At B the distance is (x − 20): tan 60° = h/(x − 20) ⇒ √3 = x/(x − 20) ⇒ √3(x − 20) = x. [1]
